executiveComp.source: Form 990 FY2024 via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer for Baptist Health System Inc (EIN 59-2487136): Mayo reported $2,400,699 compensation + $0 related + $55,718 other. Mayo also reported $1,457,401 compensation + $50,534 other on Southern Baptist Hospital of Florida Inc (EIN 59-0747311) Form 990, suggesting total cross-entity compensation may reach ~$3.9M. Former CEO Brett S. McClung received $2,130,059 + $11,393 other before resignation effective May 1, 2021. Mayo retiring January 16, 2026; Matthew A. Zuino (COO since 2020) named successor effective January 17, 2026.

communityBenefit.source: Lown Hospitals Index ranks Baptist Medical Center Jacksonville 68th out of 159 Florida hospitals on community benefit. Baptist Health provides free care for uninsured patients with household income below 3x federal poverty guidelines. Florida 340B hospitals provide 4.1% charity care vs 2.28% national average. 45% of Florida private nonprofit hospitals had a 'fair share deficit' (2020-2022), with a total deficit of $485M/year statewide (Lown Institute). System-level community benefit dollar amount not separately confirmed for Jacksonville entity vs Baptist Health South Florida.

taxAdvantage.notes: Baptist Health operates five hospitals and numerous clinics across Northeast Florida, all property-tax-exempt. Florida has no state personal income tax but does levy a corporate income tax (5.5%) from which Baptist Health is exempt. Federal income tax foregone on $530.9M net surplus (SBHF FY2024) would be substantial at 21% rate (~$111M). Tax-exempt bond interest subsidy applies to outstanding Series 2007A, 2015, and 2022 debt. 340B program participation as DSH provides additional drug discount revenue.

layoffs.notes: Jacksonville Orthopaedic Institute (Baptist Health-affiliated) laying off 306 employees and closing 6 clinics between May 30 and July 13, 2025. Restructuring followed JOI physicians repurchasing stock originally sold to Baptist Health in 2011. Affected roles include physicians, radiology technologists, medical secretaries, patient account representatives, appointment schedulers, and medical assistants.

accusation: Baptist Health's hospital subsidiary posted a $530 million net surplus on $2.6 billion in revenue in FY2024 while the parent entity held $750 million in assets and the system foundation another $369 million, yet its decade-long orthopedic partnership with Jacksonville Orthopaedic Institute ended with 306 layoffs and six clinic closures, and the system's community benefit spending ranks only 68th out of 159 Florida hospitals.
